oppango (obp- ), pēgi, pactum, 3, v. a. ob-pango,
I.to fasten or fix on, to affix (anteclass. and in post-Aug. prose): “ubi savium oppegit, fugit,” imprinted, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 60 : repagula, quae ... ex contrario oppanguntur, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. repagula, p. 281 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
